speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me. I understand you have increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with episodes of pain when urinating. You also mentioned a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own. Could you tell me how long these knee and urinary symptoms have been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome). The clinical presentation of a triad involving asymmetric oligoarthritis (ankle and knee), urethritis, and a history of recent sexual activity is highly suggestive of this condition, likely triggered by an infection. I recommend ordering a Urinalysis, Urine Culture, and HLA-B27 testing to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes.
